title: Photocatalytic removal of textile wastewater-originated methylene blue and malachite green dyes using spent black tea extract-coated silver nanoparticles

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract states malachite green was reduced by 33.3% and 60% (for room light and sunlight conditions respectively). However, the Fig. 10 description table reports different values for malachite green: 30.43% (room light) and 43.47% (sunlight). This is a discrepancy of 2.87 percentage points for room light and 16.53 percentage points for sunlight. Notably, methylene blue percentages match precisely between Abstract (25%, 58.3%) and Fig. 10 (25%, 58.3%), which makes the malachite green mismatch more conspicuous. The Abstract's 60% sunlight degradation vs Fig. 10's 43.47% represents a substantial difference that could affect the paper's headline conclusion about malachite green removal efficacy.

Cross-section consistency check confirms the malachite green degradation percentage mismatch between Abstract (33.3%, 60%) and the Results section Fig. 10 description (30.43%, 43.47%). While methylene blue values are internally consistent across sections, the malachite green values diverge significantly. The Abstract claims 60% sunlight-driven degradation of malachite green, whereas the results figure shows only 43.47% — a 16.5 percentage point difference that is not explained anywhere in the paper.

summary:
Verification of this Scientific Reports paper (DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-85894-3) on photocatalytic dye removal using spent black tea extract-coated silver nanoparticles (SBT-AgNPs) was conducted in exhaustive mode with lenient strictness. The paper was segmented into approximately 35 snippets (sections, figures, and tables) and routed to specialist verifiers for text consistency, statistical reporting, citation accuracy, and cross-section consistency.

KEY FINDING — Malachite Green Percentage Discrepancy: The Abstract reports malachite green degradation of 33.3% (room light) and 60% (sunlight), but the Results section's Fig. 10 description reports 30.43% and 43.47% for the same conditions. The difference is particularly large for sunlight (16.5 percentage points). Methylene blue values are consistent across sections (25% room light, 58.3% sunlight), which makes the malachite green mismatch more conspicuous.

POSITIVE FINDINGS: (1) All verified citations (Qing et al. 2017, Bhakya et al. 2015, Kumar et al. 2021) are real, published papers relevant to the claims they support. (2) The novelty claim — being the first study to use spent black tea for AgNP synthesis AND test on real textile wastewater — was not contradicted by web searches; prior work used waste tea extract on pure dye solutions, not actual textile effluent. (3) Text across sections is internally consistent regarding methodology, wastewater source, characterization data (XRD, SEM, zeta potential, EDX), and degradation mechanism description. (4) No fabricated citations or clear novelty over-claims were detected.

RECOMMENDATION: The authors should clarify the malachite green degradation percentages. The Abstract may report preliminary or differently calculated values compared to the final results figure. This needs clarification but does not necessarily invalidate the paper's core conclusion that SBT-AgNPs can photocatalytically degrade textile dyes.
